instructions: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 2 1/4 cups water, bring it to a boil over high heat, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until the soup is ready.
Meanwhile, cut each tomato into 8 wedges and thinly slice the shallots. Slice 3 green onions and roughly chop a small handful of cilantro. Beat the eggs in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Add the shallots and stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until soft and lightly browned.
Add the tomatoes and the salt. Stir for 4 to 5 minutes, until the outsides are soft and the wedges are starting to break down.
Pour in the broth, add the sugar and bring it to a boil over high heat. Turn the heat to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the fish sauce.
Keep the soup at a gentle simmer. Stir it in one direction with a ladle and slowly pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream. The eggs set in seconds. Stir faster for finer ribbons.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the black pepper.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the green onions and cilantro. Serve with the rice.
method_notes: No version read had 20 or more ratings. Delightful Plate leads (5.0 from 2): shallots and tomatoes softened in oil, broth added, fish sauce, then eggs trickled in while the soup is stirred in one direction for ribbons. Vicky Pham fries garlic instead of shallot and adds a little sugar; Helen's Recipes beats the seasoning into the eggs and uses spring onion whites. This one follows the lead's order, scaled from 3 servings to 4, with Vicky Pham's pinch of sugar to balance the tomato. Chicken broth keeps it from being thin; water works too. It is a light dinner, which is why rice goes with it. Check the broth and fish sauce labels for gluten.
